items.headline: Trump-Xi Summit Day 2 Key Meetings; No Xi Iran Commitment Confirmed; Tariff Truce Extension Expected; 52 Senators + 177 Congressmen Letter Constrains Iran Deal Terms
items.summary: The Trump-Xi Beijing summit entered its core operational day on May 14, with the leaders' formal bilateral meetings scheduled across May 14-15. As of this brief, no joint statement has been released confirming Xi Jinping's commitment to engage Tehran directly on Hormuz reopening or nuclear concessions. Pre-summit analyst consensus from CSIS, Chatham House, CFR, and PBS held that Trump and Xi appeared 'intent on keeping Iran war from overshadowing China summit' — a framing that materially limits expectations for concrete Iran-positive output from Day 2. On trade, markets and traders priced in a tariff truce extension and Boeing aircraft purchase announcements as the most likely output — a continuation of the October 2025 Busan summit truce framework (reduced fentanyl-related tariffs, suspended reciprocal tariffs through November 10, 2026, suspended rare earth export controls). The tariff truce extension, if confirmed, is a mildly positive market signal but does not offset the oil shock. The structurally significant new input on May 14 is the congressional letter: 52 senators and 177 congressmen wrote to Trump today demanding that no Iran deal permit uranium enrichment, stating no agreement should leave open a path to nuclear weapons. This letter tightens the deal geometry from the US side — it reduces Trump's negotiating latitude on what may be Iran's most essential demand — and constitutes a new constraint that did not exist in the May 13 brief. The inhibiting window on resumed military action created by Trump's Beijing presence remains operative through approximately May 15 (departure). No CENTCOM repositioning orders have been reported.

items.headline: Warsh Confirmed Fed Chair 54-45 — Closest Modern-Era Vote; Fetterman Sole Dem Crossover; Inherits Oil-Shock Inflation; Rate-Cut Pressure Immediate; Powell Expiry Tomorrow
items.summary: The Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as Chair of the Federal Reserve in a 54-45 vote on Wednesday May 14 — the closest confirmation vote in the modern era of Fed chairmanship. The vote was almost entirely party-line; Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) was the sole Democratic crossover, as in the May 12 Board vote. Warsh becomes the 11th Fed chair of the modern banking era and succeeds Jerome Powell, whose term expires Friday May 15. Warsh's first FOMC meeting as Chair is scheduled June 16-17. The economic environment Warsh inherits is structurally adverse: inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for five years and is now accelerating on oil-shock transmission from the Hormuz closure. Brent crude closed at $107.77 on May 12 — nearly 60% above pre-war baseline — and Portland-area regular gasoline remains above $5.00/gallon. Trump has publicly and repeatedly pressed for rate cuts; Warsh has pledged to use his own judgment and not take orders from the White House. The rate-cut vs. inflation-discipline tension that defined Warsh's confirmation debate will crystallize at June's FOMC: any rate cut in an oil-shock-inflation environment risks fueling price pressure; any hold risks White House friction before Warsh has completed his first month. His inheritance is a monetary policy environment where the primary economic shock — Hormuz supply disruption — is immune to interest-rate tools. Washington Post reporting on May 14 indicated Trump allies were warning that rate cuts 'may have to wait,' signaling internal White House calibration of expectations even before Warsh takes his first vote.

items.headline: Tariff Truce Extension Expected From Beijing; Reconciliation 2.0 Finance Deadline Tomorrow; Markets Quiet Relative to Crisis Baseline
items.summary: The Trump-Xi Beijing summit is expected to produce a tariff truce extension — a continuation of the October 2025 Busan framework that reduced fentanyl-related tariffs by 10 percentage points, suspended heightened reciprocal tariffs through November 10, 2026, and suspended Chinese rare earth export controls for one year. Traders and market participants priced in Boeing aircraft purchase commitments as an additional headline deliverable. A tariff truce extension removes a secondary market uncertainty but does not offset the Hormuz supply shock — the oil price driver is independent of tariff architecture, and no Beijing output can reopen the Strait. Reconciliation 2.0: the Senate Finance Committee deadline for submitting tax and revenue provisions to the Budget Committee is tomorrow May 15. As of this brief, the Finance Committee has not publicly released committee-level text; the search record does not confirm Crapo released Reconciliation 2.0 Finance text prior to this brief's filing. If Finance misses the May 15 committee submission deadline, it will be the first concrete evidence that Trump's June 1 completion target is structurally at risk. The DHS/Judiciary $72 billion package remains CBO-scored and cleared.

items.summary: Eleven days after Project Freedom launched on May 4, the United States has sustained no confirmed IRGC-affiliated destructive cyberattack on critical infrastructure. The Day 11 clean streak continues under the marginal inhibiting effect of Trump's Beijing presence — the Trump-Xi summit's Day 2 key meetings reduce the near-term probability of a US strike order against Iran, which in turn marginally reduces the IRGC's incentive to pre-position for immediate kinetic retaliation. The inhibiting window is scheduled to expire when Trump departs Beijing, approximately May 15. The underlying trigger environment is structurally unchanged from May 12-13: Trump's '1% chance' framing is unretracted; the two-official Axios confirmation of military action lean is unreversed; new Iran sanctions from May 12 remain operative; and the congressional letter today tightening deal terms introduces a new source of deal-track deterioration. The post-summit period — May 15 onward — is the highest-priority IRGC cyber watch window of the current cycle. CISA AA26-097A (April 7, 2026) remains operative. No updated advisory, FBI/IC3 flash, or private-sector OT/ICS alert has been issued. CI Fortify remains active across energy, water, and government facility sectors. items.headline: BLM Full OR/WA Fire Restrictions Effective Today; Fedrizzi: '2026 Could Rival Most Extreme Years on Record'; Oregon Fire Season Day 7 Quiet; 18 Days to East Cascades Above-Normal Onset
items.summary: Full Bureau of Land Management fire restrictions for all BLM-administered lands in Oregon and Washington took effect today May 14 as scheduled. The restrictions prohibit fireworks, exploding and metallic targets, steel component ammunition, tracer and incendiary devices, and sky lanterns across all BLM-managed lands in both states. Jeff Fedrizzi, US Wildland Fire Service Assistant Chief of Operations for the Pacific Northwest, issued a public statement that raises the severity bar significantly: 'We are increasingly concerned that 2026 could rival the most extreme years on record for heat and dryness in the Pacific Northwest.' Fedrizzi's framing — 'most extreme years on record' — exceeds the 'above-normal' and 'structurally certain' language of NIFC outlooks and constitutes the most direct federal official warning of the season. Violations carry fines up to $100,000 and up to 12 months imprisonment; those responsible for starting wildland fires on federal lands can be billed for suppression costs. Oregon fire season entered Day 7 with no NWS red flag warnings issued and no significant active fire ignitions in Oregon or Washington. The east Cascades above-normal onset window is 18 days away (June 1). National YTD acreage burned remains approximately 1.85 million acres — nearly double the 10-year average. The federal capacity gap raised by Oregon's congressional Democrats — DOGE-related Forest Service Region 6 fire science and pre-positioning position eliminations — remains unaddressed. With Fedrizzi's 'most extreme years on record' warning on record and 18 days to the structural above-normal threshold, resource pre-positioning urgency has escalated.

items.headline: WPA Day 15: Congressional Letter Tightens Iran Deal Floor; Warsh Chair Confirmed; Powell Expiry Tomorrow; Finance Text Deadline Tomorrow
items.summary: May 14 is WPA Day 15 past the April 29 statutory deadline — the longest unauthorized war-operation run in the modern War Powers Resolution era. Trump's physical presence in Beijing for the Day 2 summit meetings creates one additional day of deferral on any resumption order, but the structural WPA gap is unchanged: if Trump returns from Beijing and orders Project Freedom resumed, the operation would restart in an identically unauthorized posture. Senate Republicans have defeated six Democratic war-powers resolutions; no seventh has been scheduled. The day's most consequential domestic input with geopolitical consequence is the congressional letter: 52 senators and 177 congressmen wrote to Trump demanding that any Iran deal include zero uranium enrichment. The letter's signatories represent a veto-relevant Senate coalition — if 52 senators oppose a deal with enrichment, any agreement allowing enrichment would face a legislative blocking threat. This constrains Trump's dealmaking latitude precisely at the moment the Beijing summit is supposed to catalyze a new diplomatic channel. Separately: Kevin Warsh was confirmed as Fed Chair (54-45) and Jerome Powell's term expires tomorrow May 15. The confirmation resolves one of the three triple-convergence cluster elements from the week's opening — but Warsh inherits an oil-shock inflation environment that rate tools cannot directly address. Reconciliation 2.0: Senate Finance Committee text submission deadline is tomorrow May 15; Finance text has not been publicly confirmed released as of this brief. If Finance misses tomorrow's deadline, Trump's June 1 completion target faces its first concrete legislative evidence of structural risk.

items.headline: OHA Measles Wednesday Update: No New Count Confirmed as of This Brief; Last Published 20 Cases Now 22 Days Stale; First Hospitalization Day 2 Follow-Up; School Vaccination Window 2.5 Weeks
items.summary: The Oregon Health Authority's expected Wednesday May 14 measles case count update had not been publicly confirmed as of this brief's filing. The last published Oregon confirmed case count remains approximately 20 (as of April 22, now 22 days stale). The first Oregon measles hospitalization of 2026 — confirmed May 12 — is Day 2: the patient has been discharged and is reportedly recovering. The hospitalization, despite the encouraging individual outcome, elevated OHA's response urgency and raised expectations for an updated count today. Active wastewater surveillance detections across multiple counties and the multi-household outbreak spread to Multnomah and Clackamas counties both support the inference that the actual case count is materially above the published 20. Of the last published 20 confirmed cases, 19 involved unvaccinated individuals or those with unknown vaccination status. Washington State remains at 40+ confirmed cases across 8 counties, with Kittitas County in active outbreak status. The national CDC confirmed case count was 1,842 as of May 7 — now 7 days stale. The PNW school-year vaccination catch-up window has narrowed to approximately 2.5 weeks (most PNW school districts close mid-to-late June 2026). If OHA does not publish an update today, the Wednesday release window closes and the count staleness extends to the next scheduled update. The hospitalization event and 22-day count gap together make an OHA update overdue by the standards of the outbreak's prior release cadence.
